sessions.phase_label: Audit findings, scope decisions, and initial delivery

requirements.title: Release 1 Front-End Readiness Audit
requirements.definition: Provide a written review of the sufficiently built Release 1 front-end scope, including a readiness recommendation, evidence-backed prioritised findings, risk assessment, remediation effort, and explicit assumptions and exclusions.
requirements.boundary_note: The report sections, file-and-line evidence, written format, delivery timing, review-access constraints, and later Connector Module narrowing are attributes or scope changes of one commissioned audit deliverable. Product behaviors discovered by the audit remain separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Instant Connection Access Revocation
requirements.definition: Disconnecting an integration must immediately revoke access by removing the corresponding connection record and must not report success while the connection remains active.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers connector disconnection and access revocation, not revoking or removing a user from a multi-user account.

requirements.title: Invited-User Acceptance Flow
requirements.definition: An invited user must be able to follow an invitation route and complete account acceptance through the acceptance API.

requirements.title: Owner-Facing Per-Member Usage Metering
requirements.definition: Account owners must have access to per-member token consumption, usage breakdowns, and individual-limit information rather than those capabilities being restricted to superadmins.

unresolved_candidates.description: The client's detailed Slack answers are absent. Message 27 summarizes Release 1 confirmation for multi-user and instant revocation, but the precise scope decisions and the timing of owner-facing per-member metering cannot be fully recovered.
Wallet is named as confirmed Release 1 scope, but no observable message defines the independently testable wallet behavior well enough to establish a Requirement Atom.

The front-end Release 1 audit is complete. Everything is in the shared Drive folder <https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ypPB0p6dldNxhYRIiaWZfrGiGd5hjBTF> :

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Hi Andre, three scope questions from the front-end review. All three are decisions rather than defects, so they're yours rather than Anjali's.

1\. Is the multi-user scenario in Release 1? The invite send exists, but the front end never calls POST /account/users/accept and there's no route for the invite link, so an invited user has nowhere to land. Making it work end-to-end also needs member-list, revoke and remove on the backend: none of those endpoints exist today.

2\. "Instant access revocation" is in the product description, but with #1427 open the disconnect endpoints return success without removing the connection record. The front end handles this correctly and refuses to claim success, so the claim and the behaviour don't currently match.

3\. Anjali's per-member metering requirements (token consumption per member, usage breakdown, individual limits) are implemented only in the superadmin console under /admin. The account owner has no access to any of them. Was an owner-facing view planned for R1, or is that Phase 2?

value_updates.disconnect_effect: Immediately revoke integration access by removing the corresponding connection record

replacement.title: Account Member Management
replacement.definition: The multi-user account flow must provide backend-supported capabilities to list members and revoke or remove their access.

human_review.decision_note: Member listing and revoke/remove capabilities are product behaviors distinct from invitation acceptance and are explicitly reported as absent.
